- If sentiment is positive (≥0.25) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.25) and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast slope to avoid under-correction.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast to allow for lingering volatility.  
- When sentiment is high and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop — increase forecast decline rate.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3-5 days of price oscillation), model should not assume continuation — dampen trend.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from forecast mean, check sentiment for confirmation — if sentiment is neutral or negative, adjust downward.  
- If sentiment is high and forecast is flat, consider slight upward bias — but only if recent price action supports it.  
- Avoid forecasting “smooth” trends when sentiment is volatile — allow for ±2-3% noise in short-term deviations.
